title: Ethics in accounting
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:31Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T08:14:01Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point covers honest reporting, standards and audits but not keeping information private or the social and environmental effects of decisions, which the new point requires, so it is broader than the match and a new point is needed.

draft.title: Ethics in accounting
card: Ethics are the standards of right and wrong that guide how people act. In accounting, owners and accountants are expected to act ethically when they handle financial information.
transactions are recorded as they really happened. Figures are not changed to make the business look better or worse than it is.
financial information about a business and its customers is kept private. It is shared only with people who have a right to see it, such as the owner.
decisions can affect staff, customers, the community and the environment. Owners and accountants should consider these effects as well as profit.
draft.remember: Record honestly, keep information private, and think about the wider effects of decisions.

a.q: Which action by an accountant is a breach of privacy?
opts: Showing a client's sales figures to a friend
Recording a sale on the day it happened
Giving the owner the business's own reports
Telling the owner about an error in the records
a.why: A client's figures should be shared only with people who have a right to see them. A friend has no such right. The other actions are honest recording or sharing information with the owner, which is allowed.
a.clue: Who has a right to see the client's figures?

b.q: Priya owns a cleaning business in Geelong. Her bank balance is low, so she records a $400 sale in June although the job is not done until July. Which ethical expectation does this break?
b.why: Recording a sale that has not happened makes the business look better than it is. That breaks honest recording. Nothing in the case shares information with outsiders, so privacy is not the issue, even though it is a common ethics idea.
b.clue: Did the transaction happen as it was recorded?

a.best: Showing a client's sales figures to a friend
